articles.title: Katra-Banihal Rail Speed Rises to 100 kmph Across Kashmir Bridges - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Katra-Banihal Rail Speed Rises to 100 kmph Across Kashmir Bridges Breaking News Katra-Banihal Rail Speed Rises to 100 kmph Across Kashmir Bridges By Urban Acres October 2, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The maximum permitted speed on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal railway section has been raised from 75 kmph to 100 kmph, improving the operating speed of trains connecting Kashmir with the rest of India. The higher speed was tested on October 2, when the Kashmir-bound Vande Bharat Express crossed the Chenab and Anji bridges at 100 kmph, according to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. The test involved Vande Bharat Express services 26401 and 26404. The train travelled across the Chenab Rail Bridge, the world’s highest railway arch bridge, and the Anji Khad Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge. The speed increase comes more than a year after the Katra-Banihal section was inaugurated in June 2025 as part of the all-weather rail connection between Kashmir and the national railway network. The section forms part of the 272-km Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link, or USBRL, one of the country’s largest and most technically demanding railway projects. The project has been built at a reported cost of Rs 43,780 crore through the Himalayan terrain. It includes 36 tunnels with a combined length of 119 kilometres and 943 bridges across mountain passes, ridges and valleys. The revised speed limit is expected to improve the flow of train services on the USBRL network and reduce journey times for passengers travelling between Katra, Banihal and the Kashmir Valley. The rail connection is also intended to support movement for trade and tourism by linking areas that were previously outside the Indian Railways network. The Vande Bharat service operating on the Katra-Srinagar route has been specially configured for the region’s winter conditions. The train can operate in temperatures as low as minus 20 degrees Celsius and includes heated windshields, advanced heating systems and insulated toilet facilities. Seismic dampers have also been installed to reduce vibrations and improve safety while trains operate through the earthquake-prone Himalayan region. The Chenab Rail Bridge is 1,315 metres long and stands 359 metres above the riverbed, making it 35 metres taller than the Eiffel Tower. The structure has been designed to withstand wind speeds of up to 260 kilometres per hour and has an anticipated service life of 120 years. Specially developed structural steel allows it to function across temperatures ranging from minus 10 to 40 degrees Celsius. The 725-metre Anji Khad Bridge crosses the deep Anji River valley and rises 331 metres above the riverbed. It is supported by 96 high-tensile cables and forms a key link on the Katra-Banihal stretch of the USBRL. The latest speed test marks the next operational step for a rail corridor built to maintain year-round connectivity through one of India’s most difficult railway environments. articles.title: Vande Bharat Speed Boost | Chenab Bridge Rail Milestone Jammu & Kashmir
articles.content: English News National Vande Bharat Speed Boost | Chenab Bridge Rail Milestone Jammu & Kashmir Vande Bharat hits 100 km/h on world's highest rail bridge: Speed on Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section raised from 75 km/h to 100 km/h Jammu 3 hours ago Copy link The Vande Bharat train passing over the Chenab Railway Bridge, built at a height of 178 feet, at a speed of 100 kmph. Indian Railways successfully operated the Vande Bharat Express across the world's highest railway bridge, the Chenab Railway Bridge, built at a height of 1,178 feet in Jammu and Kashmir, at a speed of 100 km/h. The Vande Bharat Express also crossed India's first cable-stayed bridge, the Anji Bridge, at a speed of 100 km/h. Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared a video of it and described it as a historic moment. Following the successful trial, the maximum train speed on the 111-kilometre-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 km/h to 100 km/h. In a post on the social media platform 'X', Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, "Today is a historic day. A successful trial of the increased speed was conducted today." The Vande Bharat Express set a new record by crossing the world's highest Chenab Bridge and India's first cable-stayed Anji Bridge at a speed of 100 km/h. This will make train operations on the USBRL project easier, reduce travel time and provide passengers with a faster, safer and more comfortable travel experience. Vande Bharat services between Jammu and Srinagar began on 2 May After the Kashmir rail link was completed in June 2025, the Vande Bharat Express was initially operated between Katra and Srinagar. In April 2026, it was extended to Jammu Tawi. The number of coaches on the train was also increased from eight to 20. According to the Ministry of Railways, regular service between Jammu and Srinagar began on 2 May. In August, the Ministry of Railways said that around 81% of the network had been upgraded for speeds of 110 km per hour or more. In 2014, the figure was around 40%. Chenab Bridge - The World's Highest Railway Bridge The Katra-Banihal section is part of the 272-kilometre-long USBRL. The entire link became operational in June 2025. The Chenab Railway Bridge stands 359 metres above the riverbed and is 1,315 metres long. Anji Bridge - India's First Cable-Stayed Railway Bridge Similarly, the Anji Bridge is India's first cable-stayed railway bridge. Built over the Anji river valley, the bridge is located between Katra and Banihal. The route also features the country's longest operational transportation tunnel, which is 12.77 kilometres long. .

articles.title: Vande Bharat Express Sets New Milestone With First 100 Kmph Run Across Chenab, Anji ...
articles.content: Vande Bharat express on Chenab bridge in J&K (Pic Via X) The Jammu-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express achieved a historic milestone today (2 October) by crossing the world's highest railway bridge over the Chenab and India's first cable-stayed railway bridge at Anji at 100 kmph for the first time. The speed test marked a significant operational breakthrough for the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project, which connects Kashmir to rest of Indian railways network. Northern Railway raised the maximum permissible speed on the 111-kilometre Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section from 75 kmph to 100 kmph after ensuring compliance with all prescribed safety conditions. The enhancement was successfully tested today, with Vande Bharat Express trains 26401/26404 crossing both engineering marvels at the enhanced speed. Previously, the section operated at 85 kmph between Katra and Sangaldan and 75 kmph between Sangaldan and Banihal. The Chenab Rail Bridge, standing 359 metres above the riverbed—35 metres taller than the Eiffel Tower—is the world's highest railway arch bridge. The 1,315-metre-long steel structure forms a crucial part of the USBRL project and has been engineered to withstand strong winds and earthquakes in the seismically active region. The Anji Khad Bridge, India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, spans 473 metres across the Anji River, a tributary of the Chenab. Rising 331 metres above the riverbed, the structure features an asymmetrical design with 96 steel cables anchored to a single 193-metre-high pylon. Both bridges were inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in June 2025 as part of the USBRL project completion. Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal said the increased speed would reduce travel time between Katra and Banihal, further strengthening connectivity whilst providing passengers with faster and more comfortable journeys. The move is expected to boost tourism, trade and economic activities across Jammu and Kashmir, with the USBRL project representing a total investment of Rs 43,780 crore across 272 kilometres featuring 36 tunnels and 943 bridges. articles.title: Vande Bharat Crosses Chenab, Anji Bridges At 100 Kmph As Katra-Banihal Train Speed ...
articles.content: Jammu, Oct 2: A Vande Bharat Express crossed the world's highest railway bridge over the Chenab River and India's first cable-stayed railway bridge at Anji at 100 kmph, as the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Katra-Banihal broad-gauge rail section was raised to 100 kmph, officials said. The speed enhancement on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section under the Jammu division of Northern Railway was successfully tested on Thursday, marking a significant operational milestone for the ambitious Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Railway Link (USBRL) project. "The maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 kmph to 100 kmph," Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal said. He said the Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26401/26404) created a new record by crossing both the world's highest Chenab Bridge and India's first cable-stayed Anji Bridge at 100 kmph. The 111-km Katra-Banihal section is a crucial and technically challenging component of the USBRL project, which is aimed at providing seamless rail connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of the country. The Railway Ministry approved the enhancement in the maximum permissible speed to 100 kmph after all prescribed safety conditions were complied with by the Railways in August this year, officials said. Earlier, trains were permitted to operate at a maximum speed of 85 kmph on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Sangaldan section and 75 kmph on the Sangaldan-Banihal section. The increase in the permissible speed is expected to make train operations on the USBRL project smoother, reduce travel time and provide faster, safer and more comfortable journeys to passengers. With the enhancement, travel time between Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra and Banihal is also expected to come down, providing faster and more comfortable rail connectivity in the region. The Katra-Banihal section traverses some of the most difficult and rugged terrain of the Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges, involving deep valleys, steep mountain slopes, major rivers and highly complex geological formations. The construction of the line has therefore required extensive use of advanced engineering techniques, including long tunnels, high-level bridges and sophisticated railway infrastructure, officials said. The section has some of the country's most prestigious and challenging engineering structures, including the Chenab Railway Bridge, the world's highest railway bridge, constructed over the Chenab River near Reasi, and the Anji Khad Railway Bridge, India's first cable-stayed railway bridge. The section also has 33 tunnels. Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra on June 6, 2025. (Agencies)

articles.title: Vande Bharat hits 100 km/h on Chenab, Anji bridges as Katra-Banihal speed limit raised
articles.content: Vande Bharat hits 100 km/h on Chenab, Anji bridges as Katra-Banihal speed limit raised New Delhi: The Vande Bharat Express on Friday crossed the Chenab and Anji railway bridges at 100 km/h, marking a new operational milestone on the Katra-Banihal section of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link. Railway officials said the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 km/h to 100 km/h. The enhanced speed was successfully tested on Friday using Vande Bharat Express services. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared this development in a post on X, describing the run as ‘100 km/h over India’s engineering pride!’ and sharing a video of the train crossing the bridges. 100 km/h over India’s engineering pride! 🇮🇳 pic.twitter.com/4GlR5QJTva Vande Bharat crosses two engineering landmarks The train crossed the Chenab Rail Bridge, the world’s highest railway arch bridge, at 100 km/h. The bridge spans the Chenab River and rises about 359 metres above the riverbed, making it one of the most prominent structures on the USBRL route. The train also crossed the Anji Bridge at the same speed. Located in Reasi district, the bridge is India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge and spans the deep Anji gorge. The two bridges form part of the difficult Katra-Banihal section, which includes extensive tunnels and bridges through the mountainous terrain of Jammu and Kashmir. Faster operations on Katra-Banihal route The increase in the permissible speed from 75 km/h to 100 km/h is expected to improve the operational efficiency of trains on the section and reduce journey time. The development is significant for the USBRL, which provides the rail link between the Jammu region and the Kashmir Valley. Regular Vande Bharat services on the Katra-Srinagar route began in June 2025 following the opening of the completed railway connection.

articles.title: Train speed on Katra-Banihal section in J&K increased to 100 kmph
articles.content: SRINAGAR: The maximum permissible speed of trains on Katra-Banihal section in Jammu and Kashmir has been increased to 100 kms/hour, paving way for faster train services through some of the most challenging railway infrastructure in the region. A railway official said the maximum permissible speed on the 111 km-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section in J&K has been increased from 75 km/h to 100 km/h. He said the increased speed was successfully tested today. “Today is a historic day,” he said. According to the official, this enhancement will make train operations on the USBRL project smoother, reduce travel time and provide faster, safer and more comfortable journey to the passengers. “Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26401/26404) created a new record by crossing the world's highest Chenab Bridge and India's first cable-stayed Anji Bridge at 100 km/h,” the official said. The speed enhancement is significant for the Katra-Banihal rail stretch, which passes through some of the most difficult Himalayan terrain and includes major tunnels and bridges built as part of the USBRL project. The Chenab Bridge in Reasi district is the world’s highest railway arch bridge, rising about 359 metres above the Chenab River. The Anji Bridge is India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge. Located in the Reasi, it spans the deep Anji Khad and uses a central pylon and cable-stay system to support the railway deck, allowing the line to negotiate the difficult Himalayan terrain. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared a video of the Vande Bharat Express crossing the bridges on his X account, describing the milestone as “100 km/h over India’s engineering pride!” With the permissible speed now increased, passengers travelling between the two destinations would benefit from reduced journey times. 100 km/h over India’s engineering pride! 🇮🇳 pic.twitter.com/4GlR5QJTva Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.title: 'I was reading Hanuman Chalisa during flight emergency': Captain Smit tells PM Modi
articles.content: Punjab Newsline | New Delhi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and praised his courage, presence of mind and composure during a critical in-flight emergency. During the conversation, Modi told Captain Smit that the entire country was praying for him and that the Mahamrityunjaya Mantra was being chanted for his good health. Prime Minister said Captain Smit’s courage, judgment and calmness had helped save many lives. He added that India could take pride in being a nation where people are willing to risk their own lives to save others. Captain Smit became emotional during the conversation and told the Prime Minister that he had been reciting the Hanuman Chalisa during the difficult situation. Captain Smit was the pilot of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when the co-pilot reportedly suffered an attack during the flight. Despite the challenging circumstances, Captain Smit remained composed and handled the situation with courage and presence of mind. His actions helped ensure the safety of all 174 people on board, according to the account of the incident. articles.title: India's first orbital computing satellite launched on SpaceX Mission | Punjab Newsline
articles.content: Punjab Newsline | New Delhi India has launched its first AI-powered satellite capable of analysing images and data directly in space instead of sending all raw information to Earth for processing. The technology is expected to support border surveillance, disaster management and other applications while reducing the time and cost involved in data transmission. Hyderabad-based space technology company TechMe2Space’s MOI-1A satellite was launched at 11:48 pm aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission. According to the company, MOI-1A is India’s first orbital computing satellite, making India the fourth country after the United States, the European Union and China to develop such a capability. Traditionally, satellites capture large volumes of images and data and transmit them to Earth, where the information is processed and analysed. MOI-1A is designed to perform this processing in orbit using AI, allowing only relevant and useful information to be transmitted to ground stations. TechMe2Space CEO Raunak Kumar Samant Rai said that if a satellite collects 300 GB of data but only 5 GB is useful, its AI system can identify the relevant information and transmit only that portion to Earth. The technology could be used for monitoring floods, forests, agricultural fields, mining areas, borders and land. By processing data in space, the satellite can potentially reduce bandwidth requirements, transmission time and associated costs. articles.title: India Launches First AI Satellite MOI-1A; Space Image Processing Tech - Bhaskar English
articles.content: English News National India Launches First AI Satellite MOI 1A; Space Image Processing Tech India becomes 4th country to launch AI satellite: Processes images in space, sends instant data for border surveillance, disaster response Hyderabad 10 hours ago Copy link MOI-1A is a 13-kilogram, 6U AI satellite with a capacity of 120 watts that will process data in space itself. India has sent into space its first satellite that will not only capture images and send them to Earth, but also analyse them in space. Hyderabad-based company TechMeToSpace launched its MOI-1A satellite at 11:48 p.m. on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission. Company CEO Raunak Kumar Samantaray said that AI would be able to remove unnecessary data and send only useful information to Earth. For example, if the satellite collects 300 GB of data and only a small part of it is needed, AI can isolate and send that portion. This will reduce the time and cost involved in transmitting images and data to Earth. According to the company, this is India's first orbital computing satellite. After the US, the European Union and China, India has become the world's fourth country with this capability. Satellite to sort data in space At present, data received from a satellite is first sent to Earth. It is then examined and analysed. The new satellite will be able to carry out this process in space itself. For instance, if a satellite collects 300 GB of data and only 5 GB of it is useful, AI can identify the necessary data and send only that information to Earth. This will reduce the time and cost of data transfer. Uses ranging from floods to farming This technology can be used for monitoring floods, forests, crops, mining areas, borders and land. For example, in the event of a flood, satellite images can determine the area covered by water and then send only the necessary information to the ground. TechMeTooSpace founder and CEO Raunak Kumar, who started the company in 2023. Preparing a data centre in space in 2028 The company has also planned to build a large data centre in space in 2028. It is preparing to send higher-capacity satellites, each weighing 100 kg, for this purpose. The plan is to equip them with a large number of graphics processors and around 100 terabytes of storage. The goal is to develop the capability to analyse data in space itself by linking multiple satellites. .
